name: The Armour household at 2115 Prairie Avenue
head: pa1904_armour_mrs_philip_d

present_on_scene_date.note: Listed at 2115 Prairie Avenue in the Blue Book for 1904 (canvass begun September 1903) and again in the 1905 edition (canvass begun September 1904), which bracket 1 July 1904. The 1905 list prints: 2115 Mrs. Philip D. Armour.

associated_with.note: The Blue Book's Prairie Avenue street list prints the household at 2115, and the 1905 list again. The book gives no date the household came or went, so neither end is dated here.

not_in_this_household.note: WHO IS NOT ON THIS CARD, AND WHY. The Blue Book is a society register: it names the family members who received and were received, prints unmarried daughters only as '& dr.', and names no young children, servants, coachmen, cooks or nurses. A house of this kind kept live-in staff, and the 1900 and 1910 censuses name them; neither was read for this card, so no staff are listed. A person goes on this card when a source names them, and not before.

persons.name: Mrs. Philip D. Armour
persons.note: The meat-packer's widow; the Prairie Avenue marker says the house was 'for nearly 50 years the home' of the Armour family and that his widow died there in 1927.
